text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Miners pile pressure on government over subsidy cuts; Bonn stands its ground
- SPD sets conditions for resuming tax talks with government
- Health insurers fear higher costs for patients
- Cow infected with BSE was imported from Britain, investigation shows
- Construction industry fears slump will get worse
- Government to promote tele-commuting
- Frankfurt bourse's New Market opens strongly
HANDELSBLATT
- Bonn says it will stand firm on coal subsidy cuts despite protests
- Construction industry expects wave of bankruptcies to continue; urges more public sector investment
- Frankfurt bourse's New Market opens strongly
- Henkel to pay higher dividend for 1996
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Miners' resistance grows to Bonn's subsidy cuts plan
- Construction workers protest against low wages paid to foreign labourers
- American spy expelled from Bonn
- Patients to pay more for health services
- German railways want to axe one-third of network
- Construction industry sees 80,000 jobs being lost this year
- Russia campaigns in Frankfurt for more foreign investment
- Profit prospects in chemicals sector push shares to record levels
DIE WELT
- Coal miners take their protest to Bonn
- Opposition Social Democrats decline to return immediately to tax talks with government
- Construction industry slump conrtinues
- Construction Minister Toepfer calls for new talks on ways to keep building workers employed all year round
- Doctors and health insurers oppose Bonn's new plans on health reform
- Government to promote tele-commuting
